notes: P2.T20/T23. `shapes/ae350_soc.py`: the 149-port AE350_SOC vehicle as a ShapeSpec -- every mapped port bit on its own flop, the six named clock ports on six DISTINCT nets (CORE_CLK from the PLL pinned at PLL_R[0], CLKOUT1, per MUG1031; DDR/AHB/APB/RTC/DBG_TCK from the five stages of a ripple divider), the PLL and eight named port flops pinned by INS_LOC in BOTH flows. Scope: the block's band (row 0, cols 145-181) plus the PLL_R[0] site; the 216 ae350_config tiles and the pinned-flop tile are context (F6) -- measured, including the config tiles turns 0 in-scope cell diffs into 1515 because they are ordinary fabric the vendor fills with the design's own logic. E1 holds on the bitstream-addressed bel: u_pll realised at X177Y27/PLL, as exported. HEAD ORDER: the map carries SEVEN CLK-class input taps, not six -- INTEG_TCK is the seventh. The vendor realises six, at (0,162)/CLK0, (0,163)/CLK2, (0,164)/CLK2, (0,165)/CLK0, (0,174)/CLK0, (0,179)/CLK0 -- the same six the open flow uses -- and NEVER the (0,87)/CLK1 tap the chipdb assigns to CORE_CLK: the vendor takes the core clock over the dedicated PLL route MUG1031 describes, so that seventh entry is a fabric alternative the vendor does not use. Two taps are resolved to a port by their own source wire: CORE_CLK -> (0,87)/CLK1 from R28C178_MPLLCLKOUT1 (open flow only), and APB_CLK -> (0,165)/CLK0 driven by ck[2]'s flop at X150Y1/DFF0. The other four are driven through a global buffer that decodes to no cell, so their port assignment stays ordinal.
